summary: Feed s078_single to IDS is degraded: 74.5% of bytes are encrypted, exceeding the IDS tolerance of 60%. All other visibility checks (duplicates, one-way, VLAN, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: 74.5% of traffic by bytes is TLS/encrypted, above the IDS's 60% threshold. Traffic is being forwarded encrypted without prior decryption or selective bypass, so payload is opaque to the IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for signature and anomaly detection but cannot inspect encrypted payloads. With ~3/4 of bytes encrypted, detection coverage is significantly reduced and attacks inside TLS will be missed, increasing false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext payload; decrypting relevant TLS at the packet broker/SSL visibility layer (or filtering/forwarding only decryptable flows) will bring encrypted share below 60% and restore inspection capability.
